chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah! I have performed Zihar with my wife.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so emancipate a neck (slave).' He said, 'I have nothing.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so fast for two consecutive months.' He said, 'I am not strong enough.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so feed sixty poor ones.' He said, 'I have nothing (with me).' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I shall give charity on your behalf,' and gave him dates for feeding sixty poor ones. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Go, so give in charity with it.' He said, 'By the One Who sent you with the truth, I do not know anyone between these two mountains more in need of it than myself and my family.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So go, eat and feed your family.'

key_terms.ظَاهَرْتُ: I performed Zihar (likening wife to mother)

ai.seo_question: What is the step-by-step expiation for Zihar in Shia jurisprudence when a person cannot afford the first option?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the graduated scale of kaffarah for Zihar, highlighting the Prophet's pragmatic application of legal principles based on the individual's financial capacity. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the flexibility of expiation, where the obligation to feed the poor yields to the necessity of self-preservation when resources are critically scarce. The incident serves as a foundational precedent for understanding the interplay between ritual obligation and economic reality in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard himasws saying, ‘A man came over to Rasool-Allahsaww, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allahsaww! I have done Zahaar from my wife’. Hesaww said: ‘Go, so emancipate a neck’. He said, ‘There isn’t anything with me’. Hesaww said: ‘Go, so Fast for two months consecutively’. He said, ‘I am not strong enough’. Hesaww said: ‘Go, so feed sixty poor ones’. He said, ‘There isn’t with me (enough money)’. So Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Isaww shall give charity on your behalf’. So hesaww gave him some dates for feeding sixty poor ones. Hesaww said: ‘Go, so give in charity with it’. So he said, ‘By the One Whoazwj Sent yousaww with the truth, I do not know anyone between these mountains anyone more needy for it than myself and my family’. Hesaww said: ‘So, go, eat and feed your family’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying that once a man came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, I have formed al-Zihar with my wife’. He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Go and set free a slave.’ He said, ‘I do not have anything.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Go and fast for two consecutive months.’ He said, ‘I cannot do so.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Go and feed sixty destitute people.’ He said, ‘I do not have that much food.’ He (the Imam) has said that the Messenger of Allah then said, ‘I will do it for you.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) gave him dates to feed sixty destitute people and told him to give to them.’ He then said, ‘I swear by the One who has sent you with truth, I do not know of anyone between the two mountains on both sides of this city needier to this date than myself and my family.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Go, eat thereof and feed to your family.’”
